clue.text: Flight paid for by new partner's family

blocks.note: a flight of stairs is a set of steps
as in 'the drinks are on me', meaning paid for by me

explanation.surface: A trip on a plane is funded by the relatives of someone's new partner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flight' looks like air travel, but it is a staircase.
explanation.definitionFit: A stepson is the son of one's spouse from an earlier relationship, so he is a relative brought in with a new partner.

clue.text: Band wanting almost utter silence

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the word loses its final letter

blocks.note: utter means say; almost cuts SAY to SA
SH is the call for quiet

explanation.surface: A musical group longs for something close to total quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Utter' looks like the adjective meaning total, but it is the verb to speak.
explanation.definitionFit: A sash is a strip of cloth worn across the body or round the waist, a kind of band.

clue.text: Competitive horse level with leaders in the Epsom race

indicators.note: the leaders of words are their opening letters, so only those are kept

blocks.note: level and even both mean flat or equal
the first letters of the three words

explanation.surface: A racehorse runs neck and neck with the front-runners in the Derby at Epsom.
explanation.walkthrough: Epsom is the English racecourse that hosts the Derby.
explanation.definitionFit: An eventer is a horse trained for eventing, the equestrian competition of dressage, cross-country and jumping.

clue.text: University replaces faculty's third head

indicators.note: replaces tells us one letter is swapped out and another put in its place

blocks.note: U is the standard abbreviation for university
a faculty is an ability or skill
the third letter of the word, I, is the one replaced

explanation.surface: An academic institution swaps out the head of one of its faculties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Faculty' and 'head' read as academic staff, but faculty is an ability and head is the bony part.
explanation.definitionFit: The skull is the bony framework of the head, so it stands for the head itself.

clue.text: Shave the girl next door?

blocks.note: first meaning: a close shave, a narrow escape
second meaning, read literally: a young woman (miss) who lives close by (near)

explanation.surface: Is the young woman next door the one doing the shaving?
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is whimsical: split the answer into its two words and read them literally.
explanation.definitionFit: A near miss is a narrowly avoided accident, which is what a close shave means; the second meaning is a nearby young lady.

clue.text: Sierra had foul emissions removed with absorber

blocks.note: Sierra is S in the NATO phonetic alphabet
to pong is British slang for to smell bad

explanation.surface: A stinky Sierra car got its exhaust fumes dealt with by a filter.
explanation.walkthrough: Pong is British slang for a bad smell.
explanation.definitionFit: To sponge something is to soak it up or clean it off using a sponge, which is an absorbent material.

clue.text: Notice cutter bobbing

definitions.note: used adjectivally, as in a seesaw motion

blocks.note: to notice is to see
a saw is a cutting tool

explanation.surface: Someone spots a small boat rising and falling on the waves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cutter' suggests a boat, which fits 'bobbing', but it is a tool.
explanation.definitionFit: A seesaw motion is an up-and-down alternation, just like bobbing.

clue.text: Into walking and weather, you do tors in a storm

indicators.note: a storm throws things about, so the preceding letters are scattered and rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written; tors are rocky hilltops

explanation.surface: A hiker who enjoys the elements tackles rocky peaks even in bad weather.
explanation.walkthrough: A tor is a rocky outcrop on a hilltop, typical of Dartmoor in England.
explanation.definitionFit: An outdoorsy person enjoys open-air activities such as hiking, so is keen on walking and weather.

clue.text: Fire cosy when getting up, and attractive

indicators.note: in a down clue, getting up means the word is read from bottom to top

blocks.note: snug means warm and cosy
hot is slang for attractive

explanation.surface: A fire is cosy and appealing when you get out of bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fire' looks like a warm hearth, but here it is the discharge of a gun.
explanation.definitionFit: A gunshot is the firing of a gun; fire is the noun for shots discharged.

clue.text: Cart shortly setting off, a battle to accelerate

definitions.text: Cart shortly setting off, a battle to accelerate

blocks.note: surface reading: a cart briefly moving away
setter's reading: a cart cut short is a car, and cars setting off in a contest of pure acceleration describe the sport

explanation.surface: A cart moves off briefly and there is a struggle to get it up to speed.
explanation.walkthrough: Cut the last letter from 'cart' to get a car; the clue then pictures cars leaving the line in a straight sprint.
explanation.definitionFit: Drag racing is a motor sport where two cars sprint over a short straight course, so it is a contest of acceleration.

clue.text: Guess cryptic clue in rush

indicators.note: something cryptic is obscure or disguised, so these letters are scrambled
in means the scrambled letters go inside the next word

blocks.note: the four letters rearranged
a spate is a sudden rush or flood

explanation.surface: A solver hurriedly guesses an answer to a cryptic clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue jokes about its own genre: 'cryptic' looks like a description but scrambles the next word.
explanation.definitionFit: To speculate is to form a theory without firm evidence, which is to guess.

clue.text: Indian vehicle arriving unloaded and not returning

indicators.note: unloaded means emptied of contents, so only the outer letters remain
returning means going back, so the combined letters are read backwards

blocks.note: the first and last letters of the word
taken as written

explanation.surface: An Indian cart turns up empty and never goes back.
explanation.walkthrough: Both pieces are reversed together: 'returning' applies to the whole string.
explanation.definitionFit: A tonga is a light two-wheeled horse-drawn carriage used in India.

clue.text: Suspect the men left late, or never!

indicators.note: suspect as an adjective means dubious or not right, so the letters are disordered

blocks.note: taken as written
L is the abbreviation for left
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone doubts that the men departed late, or at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Suspect' looks like a verb, but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Tell me another is an idiom of disbelief, said when someone claims something you think untrue, much like 'never!'.

clue.text: Women collide and stall in Kent port

blocks.note: W is the abbreviation for women
to collide with something is to hit it
a stall is a compartment for a horse, found in a stable

explanation.surface: Women bump into things and break down in a seaside town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stall' looks like a verb about engines, but it is a horse's stall. Kent is a county in south-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: Whitstable is a harbour town on the north coast of Kent, famous for oysters.

clue.text: Notes heard when entering church, not electronic

indicators.note: entering means going inside, so one word sits within another

blocks.note: a hard copy is a paper one rather than electronic
as and when both mean at the time that
CH is the abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: Banknotes are heard rustling into the collection when the congregation enters church.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue lists the pieces back to front: the wordplay for the second word comes first, and 'not electronic' (think hard copy) at the end supplies the first. 'Heard' is a loose joining word.
explanation.definitionFit: Hard cash is money in physical notes and coins, as opposed to cheques or card payments.

clue.text: Tailor's odd bits used to stuff cheap bustle

indicators.note: odd bits are the letters in the odd-numbered positions, first, third and fifth
stuffing puts something inside, so these letters go within the next word

blocks.note: the first, third and fifth letters of tailor
common can mean vulgar or cheap

explanation.surface: A tailor uses scraps to pad out a cheap bustle on a dress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bustle' suggests the padded frame under a Victorian skirt, which suits the tailor, but it means a flurry of activity.
explanation.definitionFit: Commotion is a state of noisy confused activity, which is what bustle means.

clue.text: Does one pan for brass?

blocks.note: surface reading: a prospector panning a river for metal
setter's reading: to pan is to slate a play or film, and brass is slang for money, so someone paid to write scathing reviews

explanation.walkthrough: Brass is northern English slang for money, and to pan a play or film is to give it a scathing review.
explanation.definitionFit: A critic is a professional reviewer who sometimes savages a work and is paid for doing so.

clue.text: Sort of Nissan with second pair of wheels wonky

indicators.note: the second pair of letters means the third and fourth letters of the word
wonky means crooked or askew, so the letters are knocked out of order

blocks.note: taken as written, the car maker
the third and fourth letters of the word

explanation.surface: A type of Nissan car has its back wheels out of alignment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Second pair of wheels' sounds like a car's rear axle, but it means letters three and four of the word.
explanation.definitionFit: In a sense is a hedging phrase meaning partly or in one way, just as 'sort of' does.

clue.text: Farewell note that could be under the futon

definitions.text: that could be under the futon

blocks.note: ta-ta is an informal goodbye
MI is the third note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A goodbye letter that might have been left beneath the bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Farewell note' reads as one goodbye message, but it splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A tatami is a Japanese straw floor mat, on which a futon is traditionally laid.

clue.text: Shelf held up by Le Carré trilogy

indicators.note: held means contained, so the answer is inside the run of letters
in a down clue, up means the letters read from bottom to top

blocks.note: the run of letters from the end of the first word to the start of the third

explanation.surface: A bookshelf supports John le Carré's three-volume spy series.
explanation.walkthrough: John le Carré wrote the Karla trilogy of spy novels, which makes the surface plausible.
explanation.definitionFit: A terrace is a level shelf cut into a hillside, so shelf is a fair synonym in landscape terms.

clue.text: Poetic shepherd wandering lonely, avoiding lakes, mind

indicators.note: avoiding means staying clear of, so the named letters are left out
wandering means roaming without fixed course, so the letters are moved about

blocks.note: taken as written
L is the abbreviation for lake, twice for the plural
taken as written

explanation.surface: Wordsworth-style, a poet wanders lonely, minding to avoid the Lakes.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface echoes Wordsworth's 'I wandered lonely as a cloud' from the Lake District, steering away from the Keats answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Endymion is the beautiful shepherd of Greek myth loved by the moon goddess, subject of a long poem by Keats.

clue.text: Cold, say, for which one lines cape

blocks.note: the Roman numeral for one
L is short for line, doubled for the plural
a ness is a headland or cape, as in Dungeness on the Kent coast

explanation.surface: Someone lines a cloak to keep out the cold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lines cape' reads as sewing a lining into a cloak, but both are abbreviations or synonyms. The 'say' marks a cold as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: A common cold is an example of an ailment, which is what illness means.

clue.text: Have a go at empty abstracts on canvas

indicators.note: empty means the contents are gone, leaving only the outer shell of letters

blocks.note: first and last letters of the word
a ship's sail is made of canvas

explanation.surface: An artist attempts some empty abstract paintings on canvas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Canvas' and 'abstracts' paint an art studio, but canvas here is the sail of a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: To assail someone is to attack them, and to have a go at is an idiom for attacking or criticising.

clue.text: Wrong? French department's suffering with pretty random marking

blocks.note: a tort is a civil wrong in law
the Oise is a French department north of Paris, plus the S of the possessive
hell is a state of great suffering

explanation.surface: Is a teacher's haphazard grading wrong, given the suffering in a French school department?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Marking' suggests grading homework, but it is a colour pattern.
explanation.definitionFit: Tortoiseshell is a mottled pattern of brown, black and yellow, an attractive irregular marking found on cats and shells.

clue.text: Crack below bottom of statue's arm

indicators.note: in a down clue the bottom of a word is its final letter

blocks.note: the last letter of statue
a crack is a witty remark, a quip

explanation.surface: A crack appears below the base of a statue's arm.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'below' puts the first-named piece underneath, so it comes second.
explanation.definitionFit: To equip is to supply with what is needed, and to arm is to equip with weapons.

clue.text: Kiss parents when families get together

blocks.note: X stands for a kiss at the end of a letter
ma is a mother, so mas are parents

explanation.surface: Children kiss their parents at family gatherings.
explanation.definitionFit: Christmas is the holiday when relatives traditionally gather for a shared meal.

clue.text: Bishop and pilgrim fried vegetables

definitions.note: the answer names one fritter of fried vegetables

blocks.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
a haji is a Muslim who has made the pilgrimage to Mecca

explanation.surface: A bishop and a pilgrim tuck into a plate of fried veg.
explanation.walkthrough: A haji (or hajji) is someone who has completed the hajj to Mecca.
explanation.definitionFit: A bhaji is an Indian snack of vegetables such as onion fried in spiced gram-flour batter.

clue.text: Far too much elastic and gold stitching

indicators.note: elastic means stretchy and pliable, so the letters can be bent into a new order

blocks.note: the three letters rearranged
Au is the chemical symbol for gold
a seam is a line of stitching

explanation.surface: A garment has an excessive amount of elastic and gold thread sewn in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Elastic' looks like a fabric being sewn in, but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Ad nauseam is Latin for 'to sickness', describing something done so much it becomes tiresome.

clue.text: Always the same outside, minus ten

indicators.note: minus means take away, so a letter is removed from the word

blocks.note: external means on the outside
X is the Roman numeral for ten

explanation.surface: Things are permanently unchanged on the outside, apart from a ten.
explanation.definitionFit: Something eternal lasts for ever without changing, so it is perpetually unaltered.

clue.text: Outings old mate suggests

blocks.note: an ex is a former partner
to pose a question is to put it forward or suggest it

explanation.surface: A former partner proposes some trips out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outings' looks like excursions, but it means revelations of secrets.
explanation.definitionFit: An exposé is a public revelation of wrongdoing, and outing someone is publicly revealing their secret.
